t.E555.agn: In 2008, EFSA set a tolerable weekly intake (TWI) of 1 mg/kg body weight and reported that this limit may be exceeded in a significant part of the European population. The main sources are cereals, vegetables and beverages; the contribution of additives could not be quantified.
t.E555.body: Aluminium is very poorly absorbed from food (about 0.1%), but the absorbed part may accumulate in tissues, especially bone.
t.E555.eff.0.t: Aluminium from all sources may exceed the weekly limit; the absorbed part may accumulate in tissues. The contribution of additives could not be quantified
t.E555.eff.0.w: A significant part of the European population
t.E555.prod: It is potassium aluminium silicate obtained from the natural mineral mica (muscovite).
t.E555.regx.0: Weekly limit for the whole diet of 1 mg/kg; may be exceeded in part of the population.
t.E555.summary: A mineral containing aluminium, also known as mica. It is the carrier for pigments that give a pearlescent effect in confectionery coatings.
t.E555.what: It prevents caking in powdered foods; it is a carrier in coatings.
